We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or aniline with extra amine?). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: target amide formed from carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline with NH2). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O) (attached to aromatic ring). Actually the acid is something like c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)NH-Ph-NH2?) Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the acid side is the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Let's parse target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a tolyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which has a side chain /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the sulfonamide is between tolyl amine (para to methyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring. So step 3: sulfonamide formation between aniline (tolyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl). So precursor: tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar is phenyl bearing the α,β-unsaturated acid side chain.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> disconnect sulfonamide: gives two fragments:
A) p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1)
B) sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2

Now B can be obtained via sulfonyl chloride formation from sulfonic acid? But we can just consider sulfonyl chloride as available.

Next, B contains the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl with amide. Disconnection of amide: gives acid fragment: /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So acid precursor: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Actually the acid is attached to the same phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl). So we have phenyl ring with side chain /C=C/COOH. This can be made via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid.

Thus step 2: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). The aldehyde is phenyl with sulfonyl substituent? Wait the aldehyde is on the same phenyl that later will have sulfonyl group attached. The sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl via sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-). In B, the sulfonyl chloride is attached to that phenyl. So the phenyl ring in B has both sulfonyl chloride and the side chain. The sulfonyl chloride is attached at para? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) at position where the side chain is also attached? Actually the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonamide attaches to phenyl (c2ccc...cc2) at position 1 (connected to N). The side chain /C=C/... is at position 4 (para). So the phenyl has two substituents: sulfonyl attached to N (coming from tolyl amine) and the side chain at para.

Thus the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (para side chain). So we need to generate that via Doebner from aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para aldehyde) with malonic acid, giving the unsaturated acid.

Thus step 2: aromatic aldehyde (para-aldehyde phenyl) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). The aldehyde is 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl via S(=O)2Cl at position 1. So the aldehyde must have that sulfonyl chloride already attached. So aldehyde: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2. That's a sulfonyl chloride bearing aldehyde para.

Thus step 2: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2 + malonic acid -> ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2.

Step 1: amide formation: acid (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Thus overall three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with hierarchy: root molecule target, then reaction nodes with template IDs. We need to find template IDs for each transformation.

We can search for templates for sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). Use search with functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides, broken: primary amines? Let's try.
